Tariffs land on the world's longest undefended border. A strait gets called "American territory." Poland starts digging.

Five stories where the line being asserted wasn't a border at all.

5 ways the map moved — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ A 50% US tariff on $20bn of Canadian goods took effect after talks collapsed. Carney will match it "dollar for dollar" (BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, NYT).

The 8,891 km line was drawn in 1818 and 1846 as a parallel of latitude. Nothing about it is fortified.

2/ Trump called the Strait of Hormuz "an American territory" at a rally, as the US blockade of Iranian shipping continues (Guardian, Al Jazeera).

Hormuz isn't open water. The lanes run through Omani territorial sea, under transit rules that belong to no navy.

3/ Israel re-established a closed West Bank settlement — 30 families (BBC). Settler attacks in Areas A and B have nearly doubled since 2025 (Guardian). A 17-year-old was shot dead; accounts diverge (Al Jazeera, NYT).

Oslo II left Area C at ~60%. The roads decide the rest.

4/ 16 killed in a double-tap drone strike on a mall in Kryvyi Rih (BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, NYT).

Meanwhile DW — alone in our feeds — reports German sappers helping Poland build the "East Shield" along its northern and eastern borders since June.

5/ 20 deportees flown to Liberia, first of up to 1,200; five resisted and were flown on to Equatorial Guinea (Guardian, NYT).

Liberia was founded in 1822 as a settlement for freed African Americans. Its capital is named for a US president.

The historical parallel — Poland's borders, four outlines on one map.

1596: the Commonwealth reaching deep into Belarus and Ukraine. 1939: narrower. 1945: the whole country slid west.

The East Shield is the first time that eastern edge is fortified by choice.

Full issue — five stories, five maps, every source linked — in Lines & Legends.
